name: bit7z
listed_description: A C++ static library offering a clean and simple interface to the 7-zip shared libraries.
reason: No numbers anywhere reachable. The README (MPL-2.0, 857 stars) claims no speed: it lists formats, features (memory and stream compression, callbacks) and build requirements, and the repo root holds .github, cmake, docs, include, src and tests with no benchmark directory. The wiki lists API pages (Basic Usage, Advanced Usage, Building) and no performance page among the roughly 44 titles shown (29 more were hidden by the page and not checked). CHANGELOG.md returned 404. A WebSearch for bit7z against the 7z command line, libarchive or minizip found no benchmark; the library is a wrapper over 7z.dll/7z.so, so its throughput is that of 7-Zip's codecs and it competes on API convenience, not speed.

name: KArchive
listed_description: A library for creating, reading, writing and manipulating file archives like zip and tar. It also provides transparent compression and decompression of data, using formats like gzip, via a subclass of QIODevice.
reason: No speed claim and no numbers. api.kde.org is blocked here (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so the API index could not be read; the GitHub mirror KDE/karchive (61 stars, 1,210 commits, REUSE licensing with a LICENSES directory, described as 'Qt addon providing access to numerous types of archives') has a README with no performance wording, and tests/ (k7ziptest, kartest, krcctest, ktartest, kziptest) and autotests/ (karchivetest, kcompressiondevicetest, kfiltertest, klimitediodevicetest) hold functional tests, none named for benchmarks. A WebSearch for a KArchive or KZip comparison with libzip, minizip or QuaZip found nothing (the 'KZip' hits were an unrelated miniz wrapper).

name: Minizip
listed_description: Zlib with latest bug fixes that supports PKWARE disk spanning, AES encryption, and IO buffering.
reason: No numbers. github.com/nmoinvaz/minizip opens as zlib-ng/minizip-ng (same repo, same 'Fork of the popular zip manipulation library found in the zlib distribution' description), so this is the old name of the minizip-ng entry. The only performance wording is the feature bullet 'Buffered streaming for improved I/O performance' with no figures, and the version table says the 1.2 branch added 'I/O buffering' to the original minizip. Treat as a duplicate of minizip-ng if a record is ever written.

name: minizip-ng
listed_description: Fork of the popular zip manipulation library found in the zlib distribution.
reason: No numbers anywhere reachable. The README (zlib licence, about 1.5k stars, 2,462 commits on develop) lists features and one unquantified bullet, 'Buffered streaming for improved I/O performance'; root holds doc/ (API pages for mz_zip, mz_strm and friends), test/ and the sources, with no benchmark directory and no CHANGELOG.md (404). The repo page says the original zlib contrib minizip was unmaintained and the code was refactored and rewritten; the project makes no comparison with libzip, minizip or 7-Zip. A WebSearch for minizip-ng against libzip, minizip or 7-Zip returned no benchmark (a 2019 marksblogg post on faster ZIP decompression covers Info-ZIP unzip and 7-Zip, not minizip-ng).

name: PhysicsFS
listed_description: A library to provide abstract access to various archives. It is intended for use in video games, and the design was somewhat inspired by Quake 3's file subsystem.
reason: No numbers and no speed claim. icculus.org is blocked here (getaddrinfo ENOTFOUND), so the project page was not read; the GitHub repo icculus/physfs (zlib licence, 830 stars, described as 'A portable, flexible file i/o abstraction') has a README with no performance wording, and test/ shows a single file, test_physfs.c, and nothing named for benchmarks. It is a virtual filesystem abstraction, so the natural baseline (direct file I/O or an archive library) is never measured.

name: Zopfli
listed_description: A compression library that performs very good but slow deflate/zlib compression.
reason: Slower than its baseline by design, so no faster-than record. The README (Apache-2.0, 3.6k stars; folders go/, rust/, src/) says it performs 'very good, but slow, deflate or zlib compression' and carries no numbers. The only figures found are from Google's 2013 announcement 'Compress data more densely with Zopfli', seen only as a WebSearch snippet because developers.googleblog.com is blocked here: output typically 3-8% smaller than zlib at maximum compression, at 2 to 3 orders of magnitude more CPU time; third-party posts in the same search (blocked) give 17x to 100x slower than gzip -9. That is a ratio claim against zlib with a speed penalty, the same shape as the cmix and heatshrink no-evidence cases. In the catalogue, Efficient Compression Tool (fhanau/Efficient-Compression-Tool) already carries the only Zopfli timing seen (from catalogue data, not re-opened here): enwik8 gzip output, zopfli -i30 390.6 s against ECT -5 25.1 s (15.6x derived), with Zopfli the slow side.
